title: Decide whether a call site can be inlined

blocks.text: Inlining is the JIT's most important optimisation, and HotSpot decides it with simple rules the page lists:

items: a method of **at most `MaxInlineSize`** bytes of bytecode (35 by default) is inlined at any call site;
at a **hot** call site the limit is **`FreqInlineSize`** (325 by default);
a call site that has seen **three or more receiver types** is megamorphic: the JIT gives up devirtualization, so the call is not inlined. One type (monomorphic) or two (bimorphic) are fine.

blocks.text: Write `InlinePolicy` with `new InlinePolicy(maxInlineSize, freqInlineSize)`, `InlinePolicy.defaults()` (35 and 325), and `decide(bytecodeSize, hot, receiverTypes)` returning the nested enum `Decision { INLINE, TOO_BIG, MEGAMORPHIC }`. Check the receiver types first.

cases.says: With the default limits a 4-byte method inlines, the page's 36-byte method inlines at a hot site, a 2,000-byte method is too big even when hot, and a call site with three receiver types is megamorphic.
At a cold call site the 36-byte method is too big, because only hot sites get FreqInlineSize.
A method of exactly MaxInlineSize bytes inlines at a cold site, and one of exactly FreqInlineSize bytes at a hot site; one byte more does not.
A bimorphic call site (two receiver types) can still inline; only three or more types make it megamorphic.
A policy built with limits 10 and 100 uses them instead of 35 and 325.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: HotSpot inlines methods of at most MaxInlineSize bytes (35) at any call site and up to FreqInlineSize bytes (325) at hot ones, so small methods make abstraction free.
A call site that has seen one or two receiver types can be devirtualized and inlined, but three or more make it megamorphic.
